scenes.headline: How Dust trains a transformer without backprop
scenes.sub: Activation noise, per-token rewards, and backprop's own outer product.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Marlow! Dust pretrains a transformer from loss values alone, with no backward pass. Here is how it still gets a gradient.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Jitter each layer's outputs at every token, reward each token's noise by its own loss change, and every token becomes a population member.
scenes.mark: every token becomes a population member
scenes.say: Jitter activations, not weights, and score each token's noise by that token's own loss. Then every token is a population member.

left.title: Weight-space ES
left.say: Classic evolution strategies perturb the weights. Each member costs a forward pass, and the noise grows with every weight.

right.title: Dust
items: Search per reward is one layer wide
right.say: Dust perturbs a layer's outputs instead, so one pass scores thousands of tokens at once.

steps.say: Take one linear layer. Its input is cached from the clean forward pass.
Add a little random noise to its output, independently at every token.
Finish the forward pass and read the loss at each token.
Weight each token's noise by how much its own loss fell. Averaged over draws, that points along the output error.
Multiply that error by the cached input, sum over tokens, and take an ordinary SGD step.

scenes.title: The same product backprop forms
scenes.text: G = sum over t of g_t x_t^T
scenes.say: This is the same formula backprop uses.

parts.note: the output error, estimated from the population
parts.say: Backprop gets this error from the chain rule. Dust estimates it from the noise.

parts.note: the input the forward pass already computed
parts.say: The input costs nothing. The forward pass already has it.

parts.note: every token adds its own estimate
parts.say: And every token adds its own estimate.

scenes.title: Test loss at 1M tokens, lower is better
scenes.say: At a million training tokens, Dust with sixteen thousand draws lands just under backprop. The best weight-space method is far behind.

scenes.label: full-forward equivalents per update at 16,384 draws
scenes.say: The price is compute. By my estimate from the code, one update costs about thirteen thousand forward passes of work. Backprop needs about three.

scenes.text: The gradient is still backprop's outer product. Only the error comes from search, scored one token at a time.
scenes.say: So the gradient keeps backprop's shape. Only the error comes from search, scored one token at a time.

recap: Reward each token by its own loss
Close to backprop, at a large compute price
scenes.say: Jitter activations. Reward each token on its own. Close to backprop, at a steep price.
